title: Zero-Copy: how Kafka streams millions of messages per second

meta.yt_title: Zero-Copy: How Kafka Streams Millions of Messages per Second #shorts
meta.yt_description:
How does Apache Kafka stream millions of messages per second on plain hard drives? Zero-copy.

• Standard I/O uses 4 context switches and 4 data copies: disk -> page cache -> user buffer -> socket buffer -> NIC
• Linux sendfile syscall transfers data directly from page cache to the network card
• Zero user space copies, zero CPU cycles wasted copying bytes
• Kafka acts as a zero-copy pipeline between sequential disk and network

Voiceover is AI-generated. Source: Linux Programmer's Manual (man 2 sendfile), Apache Kafka Design.
meta.ig_caption:
How does Kafka stream millions of messages per second without melting your CPU? 🚀

Normal I/O makes 4 data copies between disk, kernel, user RAM, and network card.

⚡ Zero-copy uses the Linux `sendfile` syscall
📦 Data streams straight from OS Page Cache to the NIC buffer
🚫 0 copies in user space
⚡ 0 CPU cycles wasted on memory copies

Follow @stackshade for more.

Voiceover is AI-generated. Source: man 2 sendfile, Apache Kafka documentation.

scenes.say: With sendfile, the OS streams bytes directly from the page cache into the network card.

els.text: Data never leaves the Linux kernel space.

scenes.say: That is how Kafka pumps millions of messages every second without burning the CPU.
